scope: Recorded diagnostic results and source hashes. These earlier runtime policy variants are not retained as executable patches.

result.purpose: Served-source diagnostic upper bound, not shipping candidate

override.purpose: Diagnostic upper bound; not a shipping policy

limits: Three production CPU6 pairs on Controls only. LIVE_PERIOD_MS remains250.
Input latency ends at required-read upload acknowledgement, not display presentation.
The original complete input sequence, 40ms typing delay and submit completion are unchanged.
Zero-gap Refraction stress was not run because Controls already regressed in total interaction/work/frame measures.
Timing covers enter-scene, scene-idle, scene-input, scene-resize and return-to-page phases. Initial mount/font loading before enter-scene and inter-phase gaps remain excluded.
enter-scene includes the request to enter the scene and its settling work; it is not complete cold startup.

Background reuses and prepared paints count successful composites within each active phase. Background preparations count attempts cumulatively from observer installation; they may include work before enter-scene or between phases.
Background composites are cumulative. Maximum background bytes describe the largest single prepared canvas observed at composition, not resident memory or the temporary old-plus-new replacement peak.
The runtime permits one background bitmap up to 8 MiB; replacement may temporarily retain two such bitmaps.
CPU throttling leaves the host GPU unchanged.
The scene-input phase includes focus, End, all 37 typed input events, Enter, the submit-triggered capture/upload and the unchanged 250 ms buffer.

interactionCompleteMs spans phase start to the first upload acknowledging the submit-required read. It includes focus delivery and typing, and excludes the later buffer. focusAckMs and submitAckMs measure their individual event-to-first-qualifying-upload delays.
focusToLastUploadMs spans the focus event to the last same-source upload recorded anywhere in the phase; it can include later uploads after submit acknowledgement and is not interactionCompleteMs.
Input latency ends at an upload acknowledgement, not visible presentation.

Host CPU busyFraction is one minus aggregate idle-time delta divided by aggregate total-time delta across all logical CPUs. Its interval spans before browser launch through workload completion, including work outside timed phases.

Host activity includes the measured browser and other host processes. Aggregate busy fraction does not isolate external contention, single-core saturation, thermal throttling or GPU activity; load averages span longer intervals. It is context, not a correction factor or a proof of a quiet host.
Both sides require complete host activity records. These validate telemetry presence, not isolation from host contention.

Both CPU versions must reuse an existing background during input. Input-phase preparation events and prepared-background paints must be zero; the cumulative preparation count must also remain unchanged since scene-idle ended, including the intervening gap.
When evidenceKind is analyzer-fixture, observations were duplicated or altered solely to test this analyzer; they cannot support candidate acceptance or performance claims.
firstInputToLastUploadMs spans the first input event to the latest acknowledgement upload; inputDeliverySpanMs spans first to last input event. Several inputs can share one upload.
Normalized task rates use each trial's elapsed phase time and completed capture count; capture coalescing can change both denominators.
Percentage change is calculated within each matched trial, then summarized. A zero baseline has no percentage change.
Blank decodes and prepared text painters are cumulative trial counts at input-phase end. Other phase counters retain the scopes stated above.
Screenshot comparisons report PNG byte identity and do not replace the separate exact-RGBA quality proof.

result.policy: 75 ms only for first value-input burst and submission; continuous input 150 ms
